Nommon provides information, quantitative analysis and decision support tools for organisational intelligence and policy assessment. Our goal is to assist private and public organisations in creating sustainable value, by helping them make better-informed decisions in complex and uncertain environments.

We apply the state of the art in data science and systems modelling and simulation to integrate analytical and simulation models with supporting databases, offering our customers virtual laboratories to assess the impact of a set of potential strategies under different scenarios.

We work in sectors dealing with systems whose performance emerges from the complex interaction of interdependent policies and regulatory regimes, infrastructures, technologies, and demographic, socioeconomic and behavioural trends.

Nommon’s commercial operations are organised into four business units:
- Nommon Mobility Analytics, which analyses anonymised geolocation data from mobile devices (e.g., mobile phone records) and blends them with more traditional data (e.g., census data, traffic counts) to provide dynamic population mapping, trip matrices and other activity and mobility indicators. 

- Transport and Mobility, which provides decision support tools and consultancy services for data-driven transport modelling, with particular focus on the use of non-conventional data sources and on new, emerging mobility concepts and technologies, such as MaaS and CAVs. 

- Aviation, which provides products and services for the planning and management of airports, airlines and air traffic management systems. 

- Analytics Accelerator, which conceives and develops innovative projects and pilot studies in other areas, including Smart Cities and Urban Planning, Retail and Geomarketing, Logistics and Supply Chain, and Energy and Environment.

entityDescription:
Faculty of Political Science of Zagreb University is the oldest political science educational and research institution in this part of Europe and the only programme of political science in The Republic of Croatia.
Generations of political science and journalism graduates have earned their BA, MA. and PhD degrees at the Faculty of Political Science, among them current academic and high school lecturers, scholars, government ministers and members of parliament, mayors, diplomats, journalists, publishers, media analysts and PR experts.
Since academic year 2005/2006 political science and journalism programs have been reorganized according to Bologna model into undergraduate and graduate programs. The Faculty also offers 11 postgraduate specialist MA programs. Faculty also has an integral doctoral program in political science.
In 1996 the Faculty founded its own radio station, Radio Student, adding to the quality of its journalism program through interlinking of academic and practical skills and encouraging student creativity. In 2012 it was joined by Student Television, and both media are autonomously run by students, under the guidance of faculty members and associated experts. In 2014 the Faculty launched student newspapers Global.
In 2019, The Faculty media outlets produced and broadcasted a specialized media promotion programme about the Croatian path towards full membership in ESA and the forthcoming opportunities for Croatian private and public R&D sector entities within EU space programmes.

Solargis develops and operates high-resolution and reliable global databases of solar resource and energy-related weather parameters, as well as solar energy evaluation software and map products. The company builds on experience in solar energy and photovoltaics for 21 years. Solargis operates online services, integrated within Solargis web-based platform (https://apps.solargis.com), which provide access to geospatial data, maps and software for planning, financing, performance evaluation, forecasting and for management of distributed solar power generation. We support the solar energy industry with technical consultancy aimed at optimising the development and operation of solar power plants. Serving the reliable global meteorological data and energy evaluation and forecasting software, we maximise the value of solar power and enable its better integration with electricity grids.

Solar resource data is calculated using in-house developed and validated models, making use of five geostationary meteorological satellites, operated by EUMETSAT, NOAA and JMA. We use also other satellite data (MODIS and sentinels) for evaluation of surface characteristics and for evaluation of sites where development of solar power plants takes place. Besides satellite data we use inputs from various reanalysis and forecasting global meteorological models operated by ECMWF, DWD and NOAA.

Berring Data Collective is leading the global community of collaborative ocean data collection with fishers. Fishing provides an ideal ride for compact sensors, such as this one. As the net fishes it is catching data along with fish. 
Integration is more cost effective than manual or even automated in-situ ocean observation. But so what? this is only going to work where fishing takes place.
Well, therein lies the beauty of fishing for data. Fishing occurs exactly where data today are lacking. Our analyses show fishing is in the coastal seas where automated platforms can’t operate. 
It’s counter-intuitive that data are lacking close to shore, and these regions are where data is most important for stakeholders.
We are a startup operating and collaborating from Greenland to New Zealand. 
The thousands of fishing vessels going out to sea every day present a tremendous opportunity to fill the most pressing gaps in our sustained ocean observation. We provide both data collection as a service and a platform for centralized FAIR data management.
